title: DTP3 immunization, SDG regions compared, by wealth
headline: Central and Southern Asia: DTP3 coverage up 30 points since 2000
subtitle: Percentage of surviving infants who received three doses of diphtheria, pertussis and tetanus vaccine
years: Central and S. Asia: from 62% in 2000 to 92% in 2024. World: from 72% to 85%.
data_line: Data: WHO/UNICEF WUENIC via UN SDG Global Database, series SH_ACS_DTP3, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: Central and Southern Asia: DTP3 coverage up 30 points since 2000. Central and S. Asia: from 62% in 2000 to 92% in 2024. World: from 72% to 85%. Sub-Saharan Africa: 50% in 2000 to 75% in 2024; N. Africa and W. Asia: 85% in 2000 to 79% in 2024; Central and S. Asia: 62% in 2000 to 92% in 2024; E. and S.-E. Asia: 83% in 2000 to 89% in 2024; Latin America, Caribbean: 91% in 2000 to 82% in 2024; Oceania (excl. Aus., NZ): 66% in 2000 to 51% in 2024; Australia and NZ: 90% in 2000 to 92% in 2024; Europe and N. America: 94% in 2000 to 93% in 2024; World: 72% in 2000 to 85% in 2024
question: What lies behind the change in DTP3 coverage in Central and Southern Asia, and what could others learn from it?
